verses.text: Dis na revelation about Nineveh, di book of di vision of Nahum di Elkoshite.
Di Lord na jealous God, and e dey avenge. Di Lord dey avenge, and e full of wrath. Di Lord dey take vengeance on im adversaries, and e dey keep wrath against im enemies.
Di Lord dey slow to anger, and e get great power, and e no go clear di guilty at all. Di Lord im way dey inside whirlwind and storm, and di clouds na di dust of im feet.
E dey rebuke di sea, and make am dry, and dry up all di rivers. Bashan dey wither, and Carmel; and di flower of Lebanon dey wither.
Di mountains dey shake before am, and di hills dey melt away. Di earth dey heave for im presence, yes, di world, and all wey dey live inside am.
Who fit stand before im fury? Who fit endure di fierceness of im anger? Im wrath dey pour out like fire, and di rocks don break apart because of am.
Di Lord good, stronghold for di day of trouble; and e know dem wey dey take refuge inside am.
But with overflowing flood, e go make full end of im place, and e go chase im enemies enter darkness.
Wetin una dey plot against di Lord? E go make full end. Affliction no go rise up di second time.
Because dem tangle together like thorns, and drunk with dem drink, dem don burn finish like dry stubble.
One don come out from you wey dey plan evil against di Lord, wey dey give wicked counsel.
Di Lord talk say, “Even if dem dey full strength, and dem plenty too, even so dem go cut dem down, and e go pass away. Even though I don make you suffer, I no go make you suffer again.”
“Now I go break im yoke from your neck, and I go burst your bonds apart.”
Di Lord don command about you, and e talk say, “Dem no go sow your name again. From di house of your gods, I go cut off di engraved image and di molten image. I go make your grave, because you vile.”

Look, for di mountains di feet of di one wey dey bring good news, wey dey publish peace! Keep your feasts, Judah! Fulfil your vows, because di wicked one no go pass through you again. Dem don cut am off completely.
Di one wey dey smash dem into pieces don come up against you. Guard di fortress! Watch di road! Strengthen your waist! Make your power very strong!
Because di Lord dey restore di excellency of Jacob like di excellency of Israel; because di destroyers don destroy dem, and ruin dem vine branches.
Di shield of im mighty men don turn red. Di brave men dey wear scarlet. Di chariots dey flash with steel for di day of im preparation, and di pine spears dey shake terribly.
Di chariots dey rage for di streets. Dem dey rush go and come for di wide roads. Dem look like torches. Dem dey run like lightning.
E dey remember im nobles. Dem dey stumble as dem dey walk. Dem dey hurry go im wall, and di covering don ready.
Di gates of di rivers don open, and di palace don melt away.
Dem don decree am: dem don uncover am, dem don carry am go. Im maidservants dey moan like voice of doves, dey beat dem breasts.
But Nineveh don dey like pool of water from di days wey e don dey. Yet dem dey run away. “Stand! Stand!” dem dey cry; but nobody dey look back.
Take di spoil of silver! Take di spoil of gold! Because no end dey to di store, di wealth of all di things wey dem dey desire.
E don empty, void, and waste. Di heart dey melt, and di knees dey knock together. Anguish dey inside all loins, and di faces of dem all don turn pale.
Wia di den of di lions dey, and di feeding place of di young lions, wia di lion and di lioness dey walk, di lion cub, and nobody make dem afraid?
Di lion tear in pieces enough for im cubs, and strangle for im lionesses, and fill im caves with prey, and im dens with plunder.

“Look, I dey against you,” na so di Lord of Armies talk, “and I go burn im chariots inside smoke, and sword go devour your young lions. I go cut off your prey from di earth, and dem no go hear di voice of your messengers again.”
Woe dey for di bloody city! E full of lies and robbery. Di prey no dey leave am.
Di noise of di whip, di noise of rattling wheels, horses wey dey prance, and chariots wey dey bounce along,
Di horseman wey dey charge, di flashing sword, di glittering spear, plenty slain, big heap of corpses, and no end dey to di bodies. Dem dey stumble over dem bodies;
Because of di plenty prostitution of di alluring prostitute, di mistress of witchcraft, wey dey sell nations through im prostitution, and families through im witchcraft.
“Look, I dey against you,” na so di Lord of Armies talk, “and I go uncover your skirts for your face; and I go show di nations your nakedness, and di kingdoms your shame.”
“I go throw abominable filth for you, and make you vile, and make you spectacle.”
“E go happen say all dem wey look you go run from you, and talk say, ‘Dem don lay Nineveh waste! Who go mourn am?’ Wia I go find comforters for you?”
You better pass No Amon, wey dey among di rivers, wey get waters around am; wey im rampart na di sea, and im wall dey from di sea?
Ethiopia and Egypt na im strength, and e no get limit. Put and di Lubim na your helpers.
Yet dem carry am go. E enter captivity. Im young pikin dem also dem smash in pieces for di head of all di streets. Dem throw lots for im honorable men, and all im great men dem bind with chains.
You too go dey drunk. You go hide. You too go look for refuge from di enemy.
All your fortresses go be like fig trees wey get first ripe figs. If dem shake dem, dem go fall inside di mouth of di eater.
Look, your people wey dey inside you na women! Di gates of your land dey open wide for your enemies. Fire don devour your bars.
Draw water for yourself for di siege! Strengthen your fortresses! Enter di clay, and tread di mortar! Make di brickkiln strong!
For dat place fire go devour you. Sword go cut you off. E go devour you like di grasshopper. Multiply yourselves like di grasshopper! Multiply yourselves like di locust!
You don increase your merchants pass di stars of di sky. Di grasshopper dey strip, and e dey run away.
Your princes dey like di locusts, and your officers like di swarms of grasshoppers, wey dey camp for di hedges for cold day, but when di sun rise dem run away, and nobody know di place wia dem dey.
Your shepherds dey sleep, king of Assyria. Your nobles dey rest. Your people dey scatter for di mountains, and nobody dey to gather dem.
No healing dey for your wound. Your injury dey painful. All dem wey hear di report about you dey clap dem hands over you; because who your wickedness no fall on all di time?
